subject: Clarification: Cross-border data exports, DPF evidence and operational controls (VantageHealth)
body:
From: Emma Diaz <emma.diaz@vantagehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: security@vantagehealth.com, contracts@vantagehealth.com
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial RFI: cross-border controls + DPF evidence (VantageHealth)

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of our procurement/security review I have a short set of clarifying questions to help our privacy team sign off on the DPA annex and cross-border safeguards. We've already reviewed the template DPA you shared but need granular evidence for the following items: 

1) Processing locations and subprocessor list by geographic region.
2) Technical measures for KV cache and prefix caching (we need to understand how tokens are routed/stored).
3) What contractual or technical controls you apply when routing requests to non-EU regions (EU -> US fallback rules).
4) DPF/adequacy approach you rely on for EU->US transfers (SCCs + additional safeguards).
5) Retention policy for logs and prompt/response artifacts for enterprise customers.

Can you provide an itemized response and any supporting artifacts (network diagram, SOC/Security summary)? We're trying to close this before our legal window next Wednesday.

Appreciate your help — Emma
Enterprise Security, VantageHealth

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Diaz <emma.diaz@vantagehealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial RFI: cross-border controls + DPF evidence (VantageHealth)

Hi Emma — thanks for the list. We're on it. I pulled the items into a short internal plan and attached a preliminary answers PDF (vantage_dpf_answers_v1.pdf) with high-level responses.

Quick notes: 
- Processing locations: Hosted control plane (US) with model serving across US/EU regions; customers can request VPC/private deployment. Subprocessors attached in appendix.
- KV/prefix caching: caches are ephemeral per-GPU instance and encrypted at rest; prefix caching is per-request scope with strict TTLs.
- Routing policy: policy prioritizes region, then cost-tier; for EU customers we prefer EU-region serving; fallback to US occurs only when capacity/availability SLOs are not met and is logged with justification.
- Transfer safeguards: we operate under SCCs (controller-processor standard clauses) combined with contractual commitments, technical pseudonymization at rest, and contractual prohibitions on secondary use.
- Retention: operational logs retained 90 days by default for hosted customers; customers can request shorter retention on contract.

Attachments referenced: vantage_dpf_answers_v1.pdf (high-level answers), redwood_network_diagram.png (deployment topology), soc2-audit-summary.pdf (SOC2 summary). I'll coordinate a follow-up with Neha for any deep technical excerpts we should provide.

Next steps: Neha, Priyom — can you review the attached PDF and propose any additional artifacts we should share with Emma/security? 

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachment: vantage_dpf_answers_v1.pdf (attached)

---

From: security@vantagehealth.com
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Diaz <emma.diaz@vantagehealth.com>, contracts@vantagehealth.com
Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial RFI: cross-border controls + DPF evidence (VantageHealth)

Marcus — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from our privacy engineer: 

* On caching: we need the exact TTLs for prefix cache and whether those TTLs are customer-configurable per model/route.
* On logs: can you confirm what data fields are included in request logs (full prompt vs metadata only) and whether request/response artifacts are stored encrypted and segregated by tenant?
* On fallback: please describe the automated vs manual criteria that trigger EU->US fallbacks (e.g., SLO breach threshold, capacity thresholds).

If possible, could you provide a sanitized example of an audit log entry (redacted) and a one-page control summary we can include in our DPA annex?

Regards,
Vantage Health — InfoSec Team

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 11:41:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: VantageHealth security follow-ups — action items

Team — forwarding Vantage's follow-ups. I sketched recommended concrete items below so we can send a single, measurable response: 

Action items (draft):
1) TTLs and config: state default prefix-cache TTL = 30s for streaming tokens and 300s for eager prefix caches; these are customer-configurable on Dedicated/Private; Hosted customers can request config via support plan and we can apply per-tenant TTLs for enterprise contracts.
2) Logs: default behavior stores metadata (request id, timestamp, model, token counts, latency metrics) and full prompt/response is retained only when the customer opts into transcript retention; for Vantage we recommend 'transcript_no' by default and provide DPA clause to enforce. All artifacts are encrypted at rest and tenant-segregated; access via role-based controls and audit logs.
3) Fallback criteria: automated fallback triggers when regional queue latency > 2x baseline for 60s OR regional GPU availability < 10% for 2 consecutive minutes; manual escalation is documented for longer outages and will require on-call approval. Every fallback is recorded with reason and notified to the customer via the console webhook.
4) Deliverables: sanitized audit log sample (redacted), single-page control summary, and network/region diagram. I can pull the sanitized log sample from ops; Neha/ Priyom please own the audits and control summary.

Please draft the artifacts in this thread so I can send to Emma with the attachments and HubSpot link.

Thanks,
Marcus

---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Diaz <emma.diaz@vantagehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial RFI: cross-border controls + DPF evidence (VantageHealth)

Hi Emma — attaching the artifacts requested: 
- vantage_dpf_answers_v1.pdf — itemized answers and references (attached)
- redwood_network_diagram.png — deployment zones and dataflow (attached)
- soc2-audit-summary.pdf — SOC2 scope and summary (attached)
- sanitized_audit_sample.txt — redacted audit log example (inline below)
- control_summary_onepager.docx — one-page controls summary (link in body)

Sanitized audit sample (redacted):
[REDACTED] 2026-10-23T14:01:12Z | req_id=abc123 | tenant_id=TENANT_RED_**** | region=eu-west-1 | model=gptx-7b | action=serve | fallback_trigger=none | latency_ms=120

Key confirmations: 
- Default prefix-cache TTLs: streaming = 30s; eager/cache-on-read = 300s. TTLs configurable for Dedicated/Private deployments; Hosted enterprise customers can request per-tenant overrides under contract.
- Logs: metadata retained by default; full transcript retention disabled by default for enterprise; transcripts encrypted at rest and logically segregated per tenant.
- Fallback: automated rules as previously outlined; each automatic fallback generates an audit record and console webhook.

Links to artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-vantage-answers (read-only, expires in 30 days)
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/companies/1234567 (VH-2026-08-1492)

Let me know if you need any additional technical snippets or a brief on-key controls summary for legal. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call this week if that's easier.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: vantage_dpf_answers_v1.pdf, redwood_network_diagram.png, soc2-audit-summary.pdf
